notes: Ford Australia currently sells BEVs only in its van/LCV range (E-Transit and E-Transit Custom). Ford has no BEV passenger car or SUV on sale in Australia in Sept 2026 (Mustang Mach-E was discontinued locally; no replacement confirmed). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: ford.com.au's 'future-vehicle/next-gen-e-transit-custom' page lists a Trend variant with a 45kWh usable battery, 160kW motor and 340km WLTP range, which conflicts with the currently-orderable E-Transit Custom Trend/Sport specs (64kWh usable battery, 301-307km WLTP) confirmed via Ford's own spec-sheet PDF and independent fleet press (Nov 2025). Because the ford.com.au URL is explicitly namespaced 'future-vehicle', the 45kWh/340km spec is treated here as an ANNOUNCED/NOT-YET-ON-SALE next-generation update rather than the current on-sale spec, and is excluded from variants below pending confirmation of on-sale date. Pricing for E-Transit Custom variants is sourced from a fleet trade publication (Nov 2025) rather than Ford's own price list, which was not directly accessible; flagged low-confidence. E-Transit (full-size van) pricing shows some inconsistency across secondary sources ($89,990 single figure vs a $89,990-$104,990 range for higher trims); only the base/entry configuration is captured with confidence. V2L CORRECTION (Sept 2026): both E-Transit Custom variants were previously reconciled with inconsistent v2l values (Trend null, Sport true) sourced from a generic aggregator (evdbau.com). A dedicated Australian first-drive review (The Driven, Nov 2025) explicitly states Ford chose not to fit V2L to the E-Transit Custom in Australia, across both trims; both variants are now set to v2l:false accordingly. The full-size E-Transit (420L)'s V2L status could not be confirmed either way in this pass and is left null rather than guessed.
